entries.why_wrong: This line only defines the function and its parameter list — it doesn't open, use, or release any resource, so no leak can originate here. The leak comes from what happens to the file handle after it's opened, several lines further down.

This line is where the file handle is created, but acquiring a resource isn't the bug — every open file needs an open call somewhere. The leak is about what happens (or doesn't happen) to `f` afterward, not about this line existing.

This line just reads the file's contents into `data` and has no effect on whether the handle eventually gets closed. The leak isn't caused by any read/write on the handle, it's caused by control flow exiting the function before cleanup runs.

Nothing is wrong with this call itself — `f.close()` correctly targets the open handle and would release it fine if execution ever reached it. The real problem is that `return data` above it already exits the function first, so this line is dead code that never runs on any call.
